The reasoning shows that any 2‑colouring which avoids a red induced \(K_{1,2}\) forces the red edges to form a disjoint union of cliques, so the blue edges form a complete multipartite graph. A complete multipartite graph cannot contain an induced fan \(F_n\) for \(n\ge 2\) because the required matching among the leaves would inevitably create extra blue edges between the two matched pairs. Consequently, for every integer \(N\) there exists a colouring of \(K_N\) (take any partition into red cliques) that avoids both a red induced \(K_{1,2}\) and a blue induced \(F_n\). Hence the induced Ramsey number \(r_{\mathrm{ind}}(K_{1,2},F_n)\) is not finite for \(n\ge 2\); it does not exist (or is infinite). The claimed value \(3n+4\) is therefore incorrect.  

**Verdict:** REJECT.
